newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Anscor stock up on talk of proxy fight.
newsitem.headline: Anscor stock up on talk of proxy fight.

text.p: Holding company A Soriano Corp (Anscor) shares were up 30 centavos, or 8.82 percent, to 3.70 pesos in early Friday trading amid talk of a possible proxy fight between the company's major stockholders, brokers said.

"(The buying) is in anticipation of a proxy fight ... Many are buying Anscor expecting the major stockholders to beef up their holdings ahead of the annual stockholders' meeting," Spencer Yap, an investment analyst of BPI Securities, said.

Company officials were not immediately available to comment on Friday, but a joint statement released on Thursday by company chairman Andres Soriano III and his rumoured rival vice chairman Carlos Soriano downplayed the differences between themselves.
The statement said it was not unusual for the brothers to differ on "given issues", which the company did not specify.
Carlos also said he is supportive of Andres' leadership, and that "no effort is being made on his (Carlos') part to get control of the company".
The brothers along with their family are significant shareholders in the company.

Despite the statement, local investors were still snapping up the shares, traders said. A total of 7.05 million shares were traded by late session on Friday, with the share price hitting an intra-day high of 3.75 pesos and a low of 3.40 pesos.

Jose Maria Ricardo Garcia, vice president of Diversified Securities, said he expected the stock to hover at the current levels because major fund managers have decided to stay sidelined while awaiting further developments.
Some brokers said they were expecting the share price to hit as high as 5.00 pesos per share.
